AFWD.justification: it moves the input toward a reduced successor by applying the even division or the odd 3n+1 lift

AREV.justification: it descends from the lifted even value to the reduced successor after the odd lift

CLINK.justification: it composes initialization, parity split, arm work, paradox hold, count append, fuse, and closure in one flat order

ENGAGR.justification: the class is held as both contracting and surviving without resolving the paradox

EVALF.justification: the even divide-by-two case is the negative arm for an odd input

EVALT.justification: the odd input takes the 3n+1 then reduce path as the affirmative arm

FFUSE.justification: it joins the even and odd arm results into one closed state that carries the reduced successor and the held residue paradox

FSPLIT.justification: it opens the even divide-by-two arm and the odd 3n+1 then reduce arm

IFIX.justification: the step count is written permanently and cannot be undone

IMSCRIB.justification: it recognizes the input as itself, an odd positive integer, without transforming it

TANCH.justification: the terminal boundary contains the one-step descent, the held residue paradox, and the appended count

VINIT.justification: no odd positive integer, no parity arm, no first-passage count, and no closed chain exist before the object is named
